chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever says 'No, by the Lord of the Book' and breaks his oath, then upon him is one expiation."

key_terms.رَبِّ الْمُصْحَفِ: Lord of the Book (referring to the Quran)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for breaking an oath sworn by the Quran?
ai.summary: This narration from the Tahdhib al-Ahkam clarifies the specific legal status of swearing by 'the Lord of the Book' (Rabb al-Mushaf), categorizing it as a valid oath requiring expiation upon breaking. It highlights the scholarly consensus on treating the Quran as a distinct entity for oaths, distinct from swearing by Allah's name, and underscores the practical implication of a single kaffarah rather than multiple penalties. This ruling is particularly significant in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between general divine attributes and the physical or conceptual presence of the Mushaf in legal declarations.
